name: MonarchConsentPreferences
title: ConsentPreferences
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column for the content of a MonarchBottomSheet: MonarchSwitchRow (MonarchSwitch) per category, MonarchLink to the policy, MonarchButtons
summary: Privacy choices for a sheet: one switch per category of optional storage or processing, with Reject all, Accept all and Save choices, the saved policy version and time, and Withdraw consent.
whenToUse: Where people choose or change which optional uses of their data the app may turn on, such as analytics or advertising, usually from a Privacy choices item in settings.
whenNotToUse: For marketing messages, use MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox. For agreeing to the terms on sign-up, use MonarchTermsAcceptance. For what people decided before, use MonarchConsentHistory. For system permissions such as location or notifications, use the system permission request.
api: @Composable fun MonarchConsentPreferences(categories: List<MonarchConsentPreferencesCategory>, onDecide: (MonarchConsentMethod, Map<String, Boolean>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, choices: Map<String, Boolean> = emptyMap(), mode: MonarchConsentPreferencesMode = MonarchConsentPreferencesMode.Categories, globalPrivacyControl: Boolean = false, record: MonarchConsentRecord? = null, allowWithdraw: Boolean = true, now: Long? = null, onPolicyClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchConsentPreferencesLabels = MonarchConsentPreferencesLabels())
class MonarchConsentPreferencesCategory(id: String, label: String, description: String, required: Boolean = false, saleOrSharing: Boolean = false)

class MonarchConsentPreferencesLabels(title: String? = null, description: String? = null, policy: String? = null, alwaysOn: String? = null, globalPrivacyControl: String? = null, on: String? = null, off: String? = null, rejectAll: String? = null, acceptAll: String? = null, save: String? = null, withdraw: String? = null, policyVersion: String? = null, saved: String? = null)

options.name: categories
options.description: The categories in order, each with a name, a description, and whether it is strictly necessary or sells or shares data.

options.name: onDecide
options.description: Called when a button is pressed, with AcceptAll, RejectAll, Custom or Withdrawn and every category's state with the locks applied. Store the record and close the sheet here.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the content. Add verticalScroll and padding inside a sheet.

options.name: choices
options.description: The saved choice by category id. Leave it empty until the person has chosen, so nothing optional is on.

options.name: mode
options.description: Categories: a switch per category and Save choices. Choice: the status of each category and only Reject all and Accept all.

options.name: globalPrivacyControl
options.description: Whether a Global Privacy Control signal is on. Sale-or-sharing categories stay off with a note.

options.name: record
options.description: The saved decision: shows "Policy version 3 · Saved 2 days ago" and allows Withdraw consent.

options.name: allowWithdraw
options.description: Whether Withdraw consent is offered in categories mode when a decision is saved and not already withdrawn.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for the saved time, in epoch milliseconds. The clock by default, refreshed every minute.

options.name: onPolicyClick
options.description: Opens the privacy policy and adds the "Privacy policy" link under the description.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, to translate or to use the legal team's wording.

states.name: first time
states.description: Every optional switch is off; required ones are on, disabled and say "Always on".

states.name: saved
states.description: Switches show the saved choice; the record line and Withdraw consent appear.

states.name: Global Privacy Control
states.description: Sale-or-sharing switches are off and disabled, with a note saying why.

states.name: choice mode
states.description: Each category shows On (success strong), Off or Always on as a word; only Reject all and Accept all are offered.

appearance: No container of its own (the sheet is the surface): the title in the heading style, the description in the body style in the muted color, Material 3 switches in the Monarch accent with names in the body style and descriptions in the caption style, and secondary Reject all and Accept all with a primary Save choices. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web dialog reads and writes a ConsentProvider; on Android the app passes the categories, saved choices and record and stores the decision from onDecide, because consent storage is the app's. The parity map names a MonarchBottomSheet: the component is the content of a sheet the app shows and closes, as on iOS, so the app keeps the sheet's state and can close it after storing the decision; the example shows the MonarchBottomSheet. The switches the person moves are kept by the component until a button is pressed and start again from choices when it changes. The record type is the shared MonarchConsentRecord and the method is MonarchConsentMethod, as in MonarchConsentHistory. The web's policyHref and policyLink are onPolicyClick. A Global Privacy Control signal is a browser feature; on Android the app passes it if it honours an equivalent setting. The web's default wording speaks of cookies; on Android the built-in wording speaks of optional uses of data. A saved decision older than seven days shows its date.
accessibility: Each category is a MonarchSwitchRow: one element with the switch role, its name, and its description with any note, so TalkBack says why a locked switch cannot change.
In choice mode each category is one element with its name and description as the content description and its status word as the state.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets; Reject all and Accept all wrap onto separate lines when they do not fit side by side.
The policy link is a MonarchLink with a 48dp touch target.
edgeCases: Required categories are reported on and signal-locked ones off whatever the person chose.
Every decision reports every category, including ones missing from choices.
A saved decision older than seven days shows its date instead of a relative time.
Withdraw consent is not offered when the saved decision is already a withdrawal.

examples.title: First visit (opt-in)
Choice mode for a single optional category
examples.code:
MonarchConsentPreferences(
    categories = listOf(
        MonarchConsentPreferencesCategory("analytics", "Analytics", "Helps us see which screens people use."),
    ),
    onDecide = { _, _ -> },
    mode = MonarchConsentPreferencesMode.Choice,
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web shows the preferences as a centred dialog with a close button, opened from a link. Android shows the same content in a bottom sheet (drag handle, swipe down to close) opened from a button, because a modal bottom sheet is the platform's surface for a choice sheet. The title, copy, policy link, the four categories with Always on beside the first switch, and Reject all, Accept all and Save choices in that order are the web's.
parityExceptions.convention: Material 3 modal bottom sheet for a sheet of choices
